summary: RELEASE-010 made `npm run verify:feature -- --changed` runnable, and the first honest end-to-end run of the step immediately reported two REAL pre-existing type errors that no lane could previously have seen, because the tier died before reaching a verdict. why_not_just_fixed: `lib/services/account-management.service.ts` is application code in another domain's surface, is not in RELEASE-010's working set (scripts/verify.mjs, package.json, docs/DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md), and is in a shared dirty worktree with live lanes. RELEASE-010 is a verification-tooling task; it does not modify implementation code. Fixing an unrelated service's types from a release lane would also destroy the diagnostic's value as a measurement of the new gate.

how_it_was_found_and_proven.how: A scoped tsc program rooted at a file that imports the service. `lib/services/account-management.service.ts` is neither a root nor a changed file, so the diagnostics can only have come from the transitive closure — which is also the demonstration that the scoped step reaches unchanged code.

how_it_was_found_and_proven.pre_existing_proof: `git status --porcelain -- lib/services/account-management.service.ts` is empty, so the file is byte-identical to HEAD 16fb834f. The errors therefore exist at the base SHA, not in any lane's working changes. Reproduced in a DETACHED CLEAN WORKTREE at 16fb834f, independently of the shared dirty worktree.

read_of_what_the_errors_mean: Line 1015 passes a literal RPC name that is absent from the generated contract's function list, and line 1025 assigns a `Json | undefined`-shaped Supabase response to a `string`. Both are consistent with the stale generated-contract drift CP-HF-DISC-002 records, i.e. the code was written against a contract that has since moved. The type-generation ceiling (CP-089, CP-092) means the contract cannot simply be regenerated locally to settle it, so the disposition needs a decision rather than a regeneration: either the contract is stale and the code is right, or the code is stale and the contract is right. THIS LANE DOES NOT KNOW WHICH, AND SAYS SO.

open_question_is_now_closed.question_as_first_recorded: Is the code stale or is the generated contract stale? THIS LANE DID NOT KNOW.
open_question_is_now_closed.answer: THE CODE IS STALE. The generated contract is not behind: `create_post_with_context` is absent from BOTH the active chain (317 files in supabase/migrations/*.sql) and from lib/database.types.ts, so the contract correctly does not declare it.
evidence: grep -rn create_post_with_context supabase/migrations/*.sql -> NO MATCH. The only three hits in the whole repository are in supabase/migrations/archive/: APPLY_TO_SUPABASE_DASHBOARD.sql:315 (CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION), complete_migration.sql:403 (the same), FIX_FUNCTION_CONFLICT.sql:12 (DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS).

The two diagnostics are ONE defect, not two: an RPC name absent from the contract's Functions union raises TS2345 at the call site and simultaneously widens the response to `Json | undefined`, which is what raises TS2322 where the result is returned. Fixing one without the other is not possible.

AccountManagementService.createPostWithContext has ZERO callers: grep -rn createPostWithContext over the repository returns only its own declaration at lib/services/account-management.service.ts:1002.

lib/database.types.ts DOES contain a `posts` relation that the active chain also never creates. So the contract was generated from a real database that had `posts` and did NOT have this RPC. The contract is therefore not merely un-stale; it is evidence about what a target actually holds.
open_question_is_now_closed.target_caveat_that_does_not_change_the_a: DB-002 established that migrations have been applied out of band through the Management API, so a hosted target MAY hold the archived function even though the chain does not create it. That is why this has never surfaced: a staging database that happens to carry the function makes the call look correct. It does not make the code right — it makes the code accidentally alive on one environment, which is the most dangerous form of CP-109's class.

A_delete_the_dead_method.action: Remove AccountManagementService.createPostWithContext. It has no callers, so this is a deletion with no behavioural surface, and it removes both diagnostics.
A_delete_the_dead_method.risk: none identified; the only risk is that a caller exists outside this repository, which the zero-caller grep over the whole tree argues against and which the owner can confirm against its own knowledge of consumers.

B_author_the_rpc_additively.action: Author `create_post_with_context` in a new migration, with the generated contract question handled by the normal type-generation path, not by a local regeneration.
B_author_the_rpc_additively.DO_NOT_PROMOTE_THE_ARCHIVED_DDL_AS_WRITT: The archive version is `SECURITY DEFINER`, has no `set search_path`, and inserts into `posts` with a caller-supplied `profile_id` and `account_type` that it never checks against the calling user. Promoting it as written would create a cross-tenant write primitive. It also returns UUID while the TypeScript signature declares Promise<string>. If this option is chosen the function needs an explicit ownership check on the posting-as profile and a pinned search_path, and it is a `social` + `database` decision with a security review rather than a mechanical move.
B_author_the_rpc_additively.cost: a migration, a security review, and a generated-type change

options_and_why_they_are_not_symmetric.NOT_an_option: Regenerating the contract to make the error go away. The contract already agrees with the chain; regenerating would change nothing here, and the 1 MB ENOBUFS generator pipe limit (CP-089, CP-092) makes it unavailable in any case. The `linked` project is a different database and must never be regenerated from.
